about.title: About StickerHub
about.browseDescription: StickerHub brings together publicly available sticker pack content for browsing, search, and download.
about.ownershipDescription: Pack artwork and character rights remain with their respective creators and copyright holders.
about.readonlyDescription: StickerHub focuses on browsing, search, and downloads. It does not provide user accounts, uploads, purchases, or comments.

privacy.title: What this site measures.
privacy.intro: StickerHub uses limited analytics to understand visits and improve the browsing experience. It does not provide user accounts or collect profile information.
privacy.analyticsText: Google Analytics may receive standard usage information such as visited pages, approximate device information, referrer data, and interaction timing. This information is used to evaluate site reliability and navigation, not to build StickerHub user profiles.
privacy.requestsText: Search terms and request metadata may appear in short-lived logs used for security, debugging, and rate limiting. API keys and database credentials are never intentionally exposed in browser pages.
privacy.imagesText: Sticker artwork is loaded from external image hosts. Those hosts may receive normal network request information, including an IP address and user agent, when an image is displayed.
privacy.controlsDescription: You can use browser privacy protections, content blockers or analytics opt-out tools where available.

docs.introductionText: StickerHub provides API access for a small number of approved integrations. The API returns sticker pack and safe member metadata while omitting private source data.
docs.keyTitle: Keep the key on your server.
docs.keyDescription: Send the issued API key in the X-API-Key header. Do not place it in public browser code or commit it to a repository.
docs.authenticationText: All five endpoints require an API key. A missing or invalid key returns 401; excessive traffic returns 429. The health endpoint is authenticated as well, so it can verify both service availability and client credentials.
docs.paginationText: Collection endpoints return a data array and a nullable nextCursor. Pass that cursor unchanged on the next request. The default page size is 24, and the accepted range is 1 through 50. Cursors are opaque; clients should never parse them or display them as user-facing page numbers.
docs.healthText: Checks the authenticated service connection. A successful response includes ok, the service name and an ISO timestamp. Use it for deployment probes that can safely supply the API key.
docs.listAlbumsText: Lists sticker packs in cursor order. Use q to search the pack name or description. Numeric status and attr filters remain available to API clients that already understand those source values.
docs.getAlbumText: Returns one album detail object. URL-encode the product ID before placing it in the path. A valid response may include pack imagery, price text, copyright information and the recorded member count. Unknown products return 404.
docs.listMembersText: Lists safe sticker member metadata for one pack. Each entry includes its MD5 identifier and may include a display name, caption and preview URLs. The endpoint follows the same cursor and limit rules as the album list.
docs.getMemberText: Looks up one member by a 32-character hexadecimal MD5 value. Invalid formats return 400; a well-formed value that is absent returns 404. Server errors use the shared error envelope with a machine-readable code and a user-safe message.
docs.guideDescription: Review authentication, cursors, and public data boundaries, then use the interactive reference for complete parameters, response schemas, and test requests.
docs.quickStartIntro: The StickerHub API issues one server-side API key per approved integration and serves public catalog data from the current site's /api/v1 paths.
docs.accessProvisionText: StickerHub operators create an API key for each approved integration, with its own rate limit, expiry, and revocation status. Anonymous self-service registration is not available; request access and receive the one-time key through a secure channel.
docs.stepOneText: Obtain a client key from the service administrator. It is completely separate from the Turso database token.
docs.stepTwoText: Send X-API-Key with every request. Never place the key in public frontend code.
docs.stepThreeText: List responses return nextCursor. Pass it back unchanged; do not parse or display it.
docs.firstRequestText: Call the authenticated health endpoint first to confirm both the credential and catalog connection work.
docs.errorText: Every error uses one safe envelope: error.code for program logic and error.message for people. Raw server exceptions are never returned.
docs.healthResourceText: Verify the API key and service connection.
docs.albumsResourceText: Search, paginate and read public sticker pack metadata.
docs.membersResourceText: List or read safe sticker member metadata by MD5.
docs.publicBoundaryText: The API never returns aes_key, encrypt_url, raw_json, database credentials or source-tracking fields. Pack names, creators and descriptions remain in their original catalog language.
docs.referencePanelTitle: Need every field and a real test request?
docs.referencePanelText: The Scalar Reference reads /openapi.json directly and provides endpoint search, parameter constraints, response schemas, client code and Test Request.
docs.featureAuth: Enter X-API-Key and send test requests
docs.featureClients: Generate curl, JavaScript and other client code
docs.apiKeyStorageText: The Reference does not ship a production API key to the client and does not persist entered keys to localStorage.
docs.referencePageDescription: Rendered by Scalar directly from the StickerHub OpenAPI 3.1 contract.
docs.referenceLoadErrorTitle: API Reference could not be loaded
docs.referenceLoadErrorDescription: Refresh the page and try again.
docs.referenceNote: Enter the X-API-Key issued for your integration to use Test Request. Ask AI and MCP remain disabled until real backend capabilities exist.
